messages:
sec-bot: ALERT detected: high-severity SSRF pattern from legacy webhook proxy (service=webhooks-legacy, token=admin-scoped) to 169.254.169.254. See logs: `/logs/webhooks-legacy/2026-10-03` :rotating_light:

maria: saw the alert, pulling logs now. initial request path: `/v1/events` with body that included `http://169.254.169.254/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token` :eyes:

dan: is this hitting prod only?

priya: looks prod-only. I see ~3 requests from the same webhook id in the last 45m (ip 34.82.12.90). No successful external fetchs reported to customer-facing endpoints, but proxy forwarded the internal metadata request and got a 200 from metadata service.

maria: that means the legacy proxy is following redirects/absolute URLs and not enforcing an allowlist. immediate action: disable legacy webhook ingestion to stop new deliveries. can someone flip the feature flag?

jason: on it, toggling `feature.webhooks_legacy.enabled=false` for prod via ops console now. also adding an egress rule to block 169.254.0.0/16 at the gateway. running: `gcloud compute firewall-rules update block-metadata --action=deny --rules=all --destination-ranges=169.254.0.0/16`

alex: we'll need to rotate any admin-scoped webhook secrets that could have been abused. maria can you list the impacted webhook ids and owners so we can rotate and notify?

maria: yes, two webhook ids: wbh_9a3f and wbh_b72c. owners: svc-payment (team: billing), svc-analytics (team: insights). I'm generating new secrets now and marking old ones compromised.

dan: tagging security response checklist: revoke tokens, rotate KMS keys if signing keys used, and create audit entries. Does this service sign webhook payloads with a KMS-managed key?

maria: legacy uses HMAC keys stored in KMS v1; they are customer-shared but we manage rotation. I'll initiate KMS key rotation for `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/webhooks/cryptoKeys/webhook-sign-key`. command: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=webhook-sign-key --location=global --keyring=webhooks`

priya: audit logs: tagging for retention and extracting all calls to `webhooks-legacy` from 1h before first request to now. saving S3 export to `s3://sec-incidents/1765409876/`. also enabling debug-level wire logs for the proxy for 24h.

jason: containment done: feature flag off, egress block applied, webhook secrets rotated (new secrets live), KMS rotation started.

maria: next steps: 1) postmortem ticket, 2) patch proxy to enforce host allowlist and forbid requests to link-local IPs, 3) add unit + integration tests for redirect behavior, 4) RBAC change: disallow admin-scoped webhooks by default; require explicit allowlist and service account approvals.

alex: agree. also we should notify affected customers/teams and include recommended rotation steps on their side. Sec will draft comms.

dan: for post-incident actions, suggest adding an automated alert rule for any proxy request to metadata endpoints or 169.254/metadata paths. and update runbooks with the `feature.webhooks_legacy` kill-switch location.

maria: creating incident issue: INC-2026-1934, assigning PRI=1. adding action items and owners. will follow up with a short incident summary in #incidents and a deeper write-up in Confluence.

alex: thanks all. quick note: do we need to escalate to legal/ops for potential data exposure?

maria: legal notified, ops on standby. no customer data exfiltration observed in logs so far but we're treating as suspected.

priya: closing loop for now — monitoring for any retries or related webhook IDs. I'll post updates if anything else appears. :white_check_mark:
